title_en: Social Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated in accordance with the Constitution to regulate social insurance relations, protect the lawful rights and interests of citizens in participating in social insurance and enjoying social insurance benefits, enable citizens to share the fruits of development, and promote social harmony and stability.

Article 2 The State shall establish a social insurance system including basic old-age insurance, basic medical insurance, work-related injury insurance, unemployment insurance, and maternity insurance, to guarantee citizens' right to obtain material assistance from the State and society according to law in cases of old age, illness, work-related injury, unemployment, childbirth, etc.

Article 3 The social insurance system shall adhere to the principles of wide coverage, basic protection, multi-level, and sustainability, and the level of social insurance shall be commensurate with the level of economic and social development.

Article 4 Employers and individuals within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall, according to law, pay social insurance premiums, and have the right to inquire about contribution records and personal rights records, and require social insurance agencies to provide social insurance consultation and other related services.
Individuals shall enjoy social insurance benefits according to law, and have the right to supervise the contribution situation of their employer.

Article 5 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate the social insurance cause into the national economic and social development plan.
The State shall raise social insurance funds through multiple channels. People's governments at or above the county level shall provide necessary financial support for the social insurance cause.
The State shall support the social insurance cause through preferential tax policies.

Article 6 The State shall exercise strict supervision over social insurance funds.
The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall establish and improve the supervision and management system of social insurance funds to ensure the safe and effective operation of social insurance funds.
People's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to encourage and support all sectors of society to participate in the supervision of social insurance funds.

Article 7 The social insurance administrative department of the State Council shall be responsible for the management of social insurance nationwide, and other relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for related social insurance work within their respective scope of duties.
The social insurance administrative departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the management of social insurance within their administrative regions, and other relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for related social insurance work within their respective scope of duties.

Article 8 Social insurance agencies shall provide social insurance services and be responsible for social insurance registration, personal rights records, payment of social insurance benefits, and other work.

Article 9 Trade unions shall, according to law, safeguard the lawful rights and interests of workers, have the right to participate in the research of major social insurance matters, participate in the social insurance supervision committee, and supervise matters related to workers' social insurance rights and interests.

Article 10 Employees shall participate in basic old-age insurance, and the employer and employee shall jointly pay the basic old-age insurance premiums.
Self-employed individuals without employees, part-time workers who have not participated in basic old-age insurance through employers, and other flexible employees may participate in basic old-age insurance, and shall pay the basic old-age insurance premiums by themselves.
The measures for old-age insurance of civil servants and staff managed in accordance with the Civil Servant Law shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 11 Basic old-age insurance shall combine social pooling with individual accounts.
The basic old-age insurance fund shall be composed of premiums paid by employers and individuals, government subsidies, and other components.

Article 12 Employers shall pay basic old-age insurance premiums at the proportion of the total wages of their employees as prescribed by the State, and the premiums shall be credited to the basic old-age insurance pooling fund.
Employees shall pay basic old-age insurance premiums at the proportion of their own wages as prescribed by the State, and the premiums shall be credited to their individual accounts.
Self-employed individuals without employees, part-time workers who have not participated in basic old-age insurance through employers, and other flexible employees who participate in basic old-age insurance shall pay basic old-age insurance premiums in accordance with State regulations, and the premiums shall be credited separately to the basic old-age insurance pooling fund and individual accounts.

Article 13 The basic old-age insurance premiums that shall be paid during the deemed contribution years before the participation of employees of state-owned enterprises and public institutions in basic old-age insurance shall be borne by the government.
When the basic old-age insurance fund is insufficient to pay, the government shall provide subsidies.

Article 14 Individual accounts shall not be withdrawn in advance, the bookkeeping interest rate shall not be lower than the bank time deposit interest rate, and interest tax shall be exempted. If an individual dies, the balance of the individual account may be inherited.

Article 15 Basic pension shall consist of pooled pension and individual account pension.
Basic pension shall be determined based on factors such as the individual's cumulative contribution years, contribution wages, average wages of local employees, amount in the individual account, and average life expectancy of urban population.

Article 16 An individual who has participated in basic old-age insurance and has made cumulative contributions for fifteen years upon reaching the statutory retirement age shall receive basic pension on a monthly basis.
An individual who has participated in basic old-age insurance but has made cumulative contributions for less than fifteen years upon reaching the statutory retirement age may continue to contribute until the full fifteen years and receive basic pension on a monthly basis; or may transfer to the new rural social old-age insurance or the urban resident social old-age insurance and enjoy corresponding old-age insurance benefits in accordance with State Council regulations.

Article 17 If an individual who has participated in basic old-age insurance dies due to illness or non-work-related reasons, his or her survivors may receive funeral subsidies and pensions; if the individual becomes totally disabled due to illness or non-work-related reasons before reaching the statutory retirement age and loses the ability to work, he or she may receive disability allowances. The required funds shall be paid from the basic old-age insurance fund.

Article 18 The State shall establish a normal adjustment mechanism for basic pensions. The level of basic old-age insurance benefits shall be raised in a timely manner in accordance with the increase in average wages of employees and the rise in prices.

Article 19 If an individual works across pooling regions, his or her basic old-age insurance relationship shall be transferred with him or her, and the contribution years shall be calculated cumulatively. When the individual reaches the statutory retirement age, the basic pension shall be calculated separately and paid uniformly. Specific measures shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 20 The State shall establish and improve the new rural social old-age insurance system.
The new rural social old-age insurance shall combine individual contributions, collective subsidies, and government subsidies.

Article 21 The benefits of the new rural social old-age insurance shall consist of basic pension and individual account pension.
Rural residents who participate in the new rural social old-age insurance and meet the conditions prescribed by the State shall receive the benefits of the new rural social old-age insurance on a monthly basis.

Article 22 The State shall establish and improve the urban resident social old-age insurance system.
The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on actual conditions, merge the urban resident social old-age insurance with the new rural social old-age insurance for implementation.

Article 23 Employees shall participate in basic medical insurance for employees, and the employer and employee shall jointly pay the basic medical insurance premiums in accordance with State regulations.
Self-employed individuals without employees, part-time workers who have not participated in basic medical insurance for employees through employers, and other flexible employees may participate in basic medical insurance for employees, and shall pay the basic medical insurance premiums by themselves in accordance with State regulations.

Article 24 The State shall establish and improve the new rural cooperative medical system.
The management measures for the new rural cooperative medical system shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 25 The State shall establish and improve the basic medical insurance system for urban residents.
The basic medical insurance for urban residents shall combine individual contributions and government subsidies.
The portion of individual contributions required for persons receiving minimum subsistence allowances, disabled persons with total loss of ability to work, elderly persons aged 60 or above from low-income families, and minors shall be subsidized by the government.

Article 26 The benefit standards for basic medical insurance for employees, new rural cooperative medical care, and basic medical insurance for urban residents shall be implemented in accordance with State regulations.

Article 27 An individual who has participated in basic medical insurance for employees and has made cumulative contributions up to the number of years prescribed by the State upon reaching the statutory retirement age shall no longer pay basic medical insurance premiums after retirement and shall enjoy basic medical insurance benefits in accordance with State regulations; if the individual has not reached the number of years prescribed by the State, he or she may continue to contribute until reaching the prescribed number of years.

Article 28 Medical expenses that meet the basic medical insurance drug catalog, diagnostic and treatment items, medical service facility standards, and emergency and rescue costs shall be paid from the basic medical insurance fund in accordance with State regulations.

Article 29 The portion of the insured person's medical expenses that shall be paid by the basic medical insurance fund shall be directly settled by the social insurance agency with medical institutions and drug business units.
The social insurance administrative department and the health administrative department shall establish a settlement system for medical expenses incurred in other regions to facilitate the insured persons to enjoy basic medical insurance benefits.

Article 31 Social insurance agencies may, based on the needs of management and services, sign service agreements with medical institutions and drug business units to regulate medical service behavior.
Medical institutions shall provide reasonable and necessary medical services for the insured persons.

Article 32 If an individual works across pooling regions, his or her basic medical insurance relationship shall be transferred with him or her, and the contribution years shall be calculated cumulatively.

Article 33 Employees shall participate in work-related injury insurance, and the employer shall pay the work-related injury insurance premiums; employees shall not pay work-related injury insurance premiums.

Article 34 The State shall determine differential rates for industries based on the level of work-related injury risk in different industries, and shall determine rate levels within each industry based on the use of the work-related injury insurance fund and the incidence of work-related injuries. The differential rates for industries and rate levels within industries shall be formulated by the social insurance administrative department of the State Council, and shall be published and implemented after approval by the State Council.
Social insurance agencies shall determine the contribution rate for an employer based on the employer's use of the work-related injury insurance fund, incidence of work-related injuries, and the rate level of the industry to which it belongs.
Article 35 Employers shall pay work-related injury insurance premiums based on the total wages of their employees and according to the rate determined by the social insurance agency.

Article 36 Employees who suffer accidental injuries or contract occupational diseases due to work and have been identified as work-related injuries shall enjoy work-related injury insurance benefits; among them, those who have lost the ability to work after work capacity assessment shall enjoy disability benefits.
Work-related injury identification and work capacity assessment shall be simple and convenient.

Article 40 If a work-related injured employee meets the conditions for receiving basic pension, the disability allowance shall be stopped, and he or she shall enjoy basic old-age insurance benefits. If the basic old-age insurance benefits are lower than the disability allowance, the difference shall be made up from the work-related injury insurance fund.

Article 41 If the employer of an employee fails to pay work-related injury insurance premiums according to law and a work-related injury accident occurs, the employer shall pay the work-related injury insurance benefits. If the employer fails to pay, the work-related injury insurance fund shall pay in advance.
The work-related injury insurance benefits paid in advance from the work-related injury insurance fund shall be repaid by the employer. If the employer fails to repay, the social insurance agency may recover in accordance with Article 63 of this Law.

Article 42 If a work-related injury is caused by a third party, and the third party does not pay the medical expenses for the work-related injury or cannot be determined, the work-related injury insurance fund shall pay in advance. After the work-related injury insurance fund pays in advance, it has the right to recover from the third party.
Article 44 Employees shall participate in unemployment insurance, and the employer and employee shall jointly pay unemployment insurance premiums in accordance with State regulations.

Article 46 If the cumulative contribution period of an unemployed person before unemployment is between one and five years, the maximum period for receiving unemployment insurance benefits is twelve months; if the cumulative contribution period is between five and ten years, the maximum period is eighteen months; if the cumulative contribution period is ten years or more, the maximum period is twenty-four months. After re-employment, if the person becomes unemployed again, the contribution period shall be recalculated, and the period for receiving unemployment insurance benefits shall be combined with the period that should have been received but was not received from the previous unemployment, but the total shall not exceed twenty-four months.

Article 47 The standard of unemployment insurance benefits shall be determined by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and shall not be lower than the minimum living standard for urban residents.

Article 48 During the period of receiving unemployment insurance benefits, unemployed persons shall participate in basic medical insurance for employees and enjoy basic medical insurance benefits.
The basic medical insurance premiums that unemployed persons shall pay shall be paid from the unemployment insurance fund, and individuals shall not pay basic medical insurance premiums.

Article 49 If an unemployed person dies during the period of receiving unemployment insurance benefits, a one-time funeral subsidy and pension shall be paid to his or her survivors by reference to the local regulations on the death of on-duty employees. The required funds shall be paid from the unemployment insurance fund.
If an individual's death simultaneously meets the conditions for receiving funeral subsidies from basic old-age insurance, work-related injury insurance, and unemployment insurance, his or her survivors may only choose to receive one of them.

Article 50 The employer shall promptly issue a certificate of termination or dissolution of the labor relationship to the unemployed person, and shall inform the social insurance agency of the list of unemployed persons within fifteen days from the date of termination or dissolution of the labor relationship.
The unemployed person shall hold the certificate of termination or dissolution of the labor relationship issued by his or her employer, and promptly go to the designated public employment service institution to register for unemployment.
The unemployed person shall go through the procedures for receiving unemployment insurance benefits at the social insurance agency with the unemployment registration certificate and personal identification. The period for receiving unemployment insurance benefits shall be calculated from the date of unemployment registration.

Article 52 Where an employee takes up employment across the overall planning area, his/her unemployment insurance relationship shall be transferred with him/her, and the contribution payment periods shall be calculated on a cumulative basis.

Article 53 An employee shall participate in maternity insurance. The employer shall pay the maternity insurance premiums as prescribed by the State, and the employee shall not pay the maternity insurance premiums.

Article 54 Where an employer has paid the maternity insurance premiums, its employees shall enjoy maternity insurance benefits; the spouse of an employee who is not employed shall enjoy maternity medical expenses benefits as prescribed by the State. The required funds shall be paid from the maternity insurance fund.
Maternity insurance benefits include maternity medical expenses and maternity allowance.

Article 57 An employer shall, within 30 days from the date of its establishment, apply to the local social insurance agency for social insurance registration by presenting its business license, registration certificate, or the employer's seal. The social insurance agency shall, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the application, make examination and issue a social insurance registration certificate.
Where the registered items of an employer's social insurance registration change or the employer terminates in accordance with law, it shall, within 30 days from the date of change or termination, go through the modification or cancellation of the social insurance registration with the social insurance agency.
The market supervision and administration department, the civil affairs department, and the agency for the administration of government affairs and institutional establishment shall promptly notify the social insurance agency of the establishment and termination of employers; the public security organ shall promptly notify the social insurance agency of an individual's birth, death, and the registration, relocation, and cancellation of the household registration.

Article 58 An employer shall, within 30 days from the date of employment, apply to the social insurance agency for social insurance registration for its employees. If the employer fails to complete the social insurance registration, the social insurance agency shall verify the social insurance premiums that it shall pay.
An individual business without employees, a part-time employee who has not participated in social insurance with an employer, or any other flexible employee who voluntarily participates in social insurance shall apply to the social insurance agency for social insurance registration.
The State shall establish a unified national personal social security number. The personal social security number shall be the citizen identification number.

Article 59 The people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen the collection of social insurance premiums.
Social insurance premiums shall be collected on a unified basis, and the implementation steps and specific measures shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 60 An employer shall declare on its own and pay social insurance premiums in full and on time, and shall not postpone or reduce payment without legal grounds such as force majeure. The social insurance premiums payable by an employee shall be withheld and paid by the employer on behalf of the employee, and the employer shall inform the employee of the details of the social insurance premiums paid on a monthly basis.
An individual business without employees, a part-time employee who has not participated in social insurance with an employer, or any other flexible employee may directly pay social insurance premiums to the social insurance premium collection agency.

Article 61 The social insurance premium collection agency shall collect social insurance premiums in full and on time according to law, and shall periodically inform the employers and individuals of the payment status.

Article 62 Where an employer fails to declare the amount of social insurance premiums payable in accordance with the provisions, the amount payable shall be determined at 110% of the amount paid by the unit in the preceding month; after the paying unit completes the supplementary declaration procedures, the social insurance premium collection agency shall settle the account in accordance with the provisions.

Article 63 Where an employer fails to pay social insurance premiums in full and on time, the social insurance premium collection agency shall order it to pay or make up the payment within a prescribed time limit.
Where the employer still fails to pay or make up the payment of social insurance premiums after the expiration of the time limit, the social insurance premium collection agency may inquire into its deposit accounts with banks and other financial institutions; and may apply to the relevant administrative department at or above the county level for a decision to transfer social insurance premiums, and notify in writing its account-opening bank or other financial institution to transfer the social insurance premiums. Where the balance in the employer's account is less than the amount of social insurance premiums payable, the social insurance premium collection agency may require the employer to provide a guarantee and sign a deferred payment agreement.
Where the employer fails to pay social insurance premiums in full and fails to provide a guarantee, the social insurance premium collection agency may apply to the People's Court for seizure, sealing up, or auction of the employer's property equivalent in value to the social insurance premiums payable, and the proceeds from the auction shall be used to offset the social insurance premiums.

Article 64 Social insurance funds include the basic old-age insurance fund, the basic medical insurance fund, the work-related injury insurance fund, the unemployment insurance fund, and the maternity insurance fund. Except that the basic medical insurance fund and the maternity insurance fund shall be set up and accounted for on a consolidated basis, the other social insurance funds shall be set up and accounted for separately according to the type of social insurance. Social insurance funds shall implement the unified accounting system of the State.
Social insurance funds shall be used for designated purposes, and no organization or individual may misappropriate or divert them.
The basic old-age insurance fund shall gradually achieve national overall planning, and other social insurance funds shall gradually achieve provincial overall planning. The specific time and steps shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 65 Social insurance funds shall achieve a balance between revenues and expenditures through budgets.
Where a social insurance fund is insufficient to make payments, the people's government at or above the county level shall provide subsidies.

Article 66 Social insurance funds shall establish budgets according to the level of overall planning. Except that the budgets of the basic medical insurance fund and the maternity insurance fund shall be prepared on a consolidated basis, the budgets of other social insurance funds shall be prepared separately according to the social insurance program.

Article 67 The preparation, examination, and approval of the draft budgets and final accounts of social insurance funds shall be carried out in accordance with the law and the provisions of the State Council.
Article 68 Social insurance funds shall be deposited into financial special accounts, and the specific management measures shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 69 On the premise of ensuring safety, social insurance funds shall be invested and operated in accordance with the provisions of the State Council to maintain and increase their value.
Social insurance funds shall not be invested or operated in violation of regulations, shall not be used to balance other government budgets, shall not be used for the construction or renovation of office premises, or for payment of personnel expenses, operating costs, or management expenses, or be diverted to any other purposes in violation of the provisions of laws and administrative regulations.

Article 70 The social insurance agency shall regularly publish to the public the status of participation in social insurance and the revenues, expenditures, balances, and earnings of social insurance funds.

Article 71 The State shall establish a National Social Security Fund, which shall consist of appropriations from the central government budget and funds raised through other means approved by the State Council, and shall be used for supplementation and regulation of social security expenditures. The National Social Security Fund shall be managed and operated by the National Social Security Fund management and operation institution, and shall preserve and increase its value on the premise of ensuring safety.
The National Social Security Fund shall regularly publish to the public its revenues and expenditures, management, and investment and operation status. The financial department of the State Council, the social insurance administrative department, and the audit authority shall exercise supervision over the revenues and expenditures, management, and investment and operation of the National Social Security Fund.

Article 72 Social insurance agencies shall be established in the overall planning area. A social insurance agency may, as required by work, establish branch offices and service outlets within the overall planning area, subject to the approval of the local social insurance administrative department and the agency for the administration of government affairs and institutional establishment.
The personnel expenses of the social insurance agency and the basic operating costs and management expenses incurred in handling social insurance shall be guaranteed by the finance at the same level in accordance with the provisions of the State.

Article 73 A social insurance agency shall establish and improve the business, financial, security, and risk management systems.
A social insurance agency shall pay social insurance benefits in full and on time.

Article 74 A social insurance agency shall obtain the data required for social insurance work through business processing, statistics, and investigations, and the relevant entities and individuals shall provide such data promptly and truthfully.
A social insurance agency shall promptly establish archives for employers, completely and accurately record the persons participating in social insurance, contributions, and other social insurance data, and properly keep the original vouchers for registration and declaration and the accounting vouchers for payment and settlement.
A social insurance agency shall promptly, completely, and accurately record personal rights records, including the contributions made by individuals and by employers on their behalf, as well as records of the social insurance benefits they enjoy, and shall regularly send the personal rights record sheets to the individuals free of charge.
Employers and individuals may, free of charge, inquire into and verify their records of contributions and social insurance benefits received from the social insurance agency, and request the social insurance agency to provide social insurance consultation and related services.

Article 75 The national social insurance information system shall be jointly built by the people's governments at or above the county level in accordance with the unified national plan and on the principle of graded responsibility.

Article 76 The standing committees of the people's congresses at all levels shall hear and deliberate the special work reports of the people's governments at the corresponding levels on the revenues and expenditures, management, investment and operation of social insurance funds, as well as supervision and inspection thereof, organize law enforcement inspections on the implementation of this Law, and exercise their supervisory powers in accordance with the law.

Article 77 The social insurance administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall strengthen the supervision and inspection of the compliance of employers and individuals with the social insurance laws and regulations.
When the social insurance administrative department conducts supervision and inspection, the employers and individuals under inspection shall truthfully provide materials related to social insurance, and shall not refuse the inspection or provide false or concealed information.

Article 78 The financial department and the audit authority shall, within their respective functions and duties, exercise supervision over the revenues and expenditures, management, and investment and operation of social insurance funds.

Article 80 The people's government of the overall planning area shall establish a social insurance supervision committee composed of representatives of employers, representatives of insured persons, representatives of trade unions, and experts, which shall grasp and analyze the revenues and expenditures, management, and investment and operation of social insurance funds, provide consulting opinions and suggestions on social insurance work, and exercise social supervision.
The social insurance agency shall regularly report to the social insurance supervision committee on the revenues and expenditures, management, and investment and operation of social insurance funds. The social insurance supervision committee may engage an accounting firm to conduct annual audits and special audits on the revenues and expenditures, management, and investment and operation of social insurance funds. The audit results shall be disclosed to the public.
Where the social insurance supervision committee discovers problems in the revenues and expenditures, management, and investment and operation of social insurance funds, it shall have the authority to propose corrective suggestions; and where the social insurance agency or its staff members commit illegal acts, it shall have the authority to propose to the relevant department that it handle the matter according to law.

Article 81 The social insurance administrative department and other relevant administrative departments, the social insurance agency, the social insurance premium collection agency, and their staff members shall keep confidential the information of employers and individuals according to law, and shall not disclose it in any form.

Article 82 Any organization or individual shall have the right to report and complain about acts that violate the social insurance laws and regulations.
The social insurance administrative department, the health administrative department, the social insurance agency, the social insurance premium collection agency, the financial department, and the audit authority shall handle, according to law, reports and complaints that fall within their respective functions and duties; for those that do not fall within their functions and duties, they shall notify in writing and transfer them to the department or agency with the authority to handle them. The department or agency with the authority to handle them shall handle them promptly and shall not shift the responsibility.

Article 83 Where an employer or an individual considers that an act of the social insurance premium collection agency infringes upon his/her legitimate rights and interests, he/she may apply for administrative reconsideration or institute an administrative action according to law.
Where an employer or an individual, by the social insurance agency, fails to handle social insurance registration, verify social insurance premiums, pay social insurance benefits, handle social insurance transfer and continuation procedures according to law, or commits other acts that infringe upon other social insurance rights and interests, he/she may apply for administrative reconsideration or institute an administrative action according to law.
Where a dispute over social insurance arises between an individual and the employer with which he/she works, the individual may apply for mediation, arbitration, or institute a lawsuit according to law. Where the employer infringes upon the individual's social insurance rights and interests, the individual may also request the social insurance administrative department or the social insurance premium collection agency to handle the matter according to law.

Article 84 Where an employer fails to undergo social insurance registration, the social insurance administrative department shall order it to make a correction within a prescribed time limit; if it fails to make a correction within the time limit, it shall impose a fine of not less than one times but not more than three times the amount of social insurance premiums payable on the employer, and a fine of not less than RMB 500 but not more than RMB 3,000 on the person directly in charge and other persons directly responsible.

Article 85 Where an employer refuses to issue a certificate of termination or dissolution of the labor relationship, it shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 86 Where an employer fails to pay social insurance premiums in full and on time, the social insurance premium collection agency shall order it to pay or make up the payment within a prescribed time limit, and shall, from the date of default, impose a late payment surcharge at a daily rate of 0.05%; if it still fails to pay after the expiration of the time limit, the relevant administrative department shall impose a fine of not less than one times but not more than three times the amount in arrears.

Article 87 Where a social insurance agency or a medical institution, a pharmaceutical business unit, or any other social insurance service institution defrauds the expenditure of social insurance funds by fraud, falsification of evidentiary materials, or other means, the social insurance administrative department shall order the return of the defrauded social insurance benefits and impose a fine of not less than two times but not more than five times the amount defrauded; if it is a social insurance service institution, the service agreement shall be terminated; if the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible have professional qualifications, their professional qualifications shall be revoked according to law.

Article 88 Where a person defrauds social insurance benefits by fraud, falsification of evidentiary materials, or other means, the social insurance administrative department shall order the return of the defrauded social insurance benefits and impose a fine of not less than two times but not more than five times the amount defrauded.

Article 90 Where a social insurance premium collection agency, without authorization, changes the contribution base or rate of social insurance premiums, resulting in under-collection or over-collection of social insurance premiums, the relevant administrative department shall order it to recover the social insurance premiums that should have been paid or refund the social insurance premiums that should not have been paid; the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 91 Whoever, in violation of the provisions of this Law, conceals, transfers, misappropriates, or diverts social insurance funds, or invests or operates them in violation of regulations, the social insurance administrative department, the financial department, and the audit authority shall order the recovery thereof; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 92 Where the social insurance administrative department and other relevant administrative departments, the social insurance agency, the social insurance premium collection agency, or any of their staff members disclose the information of employers or individuals, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law; if losses are caused to the employer or the individual, compensation liability shall be borne.

Article 93 Where State functionaries abuse their powers, neglect their duties, or engage in malpractices for personal gain in the management and supervision of social insurance, they shall be given sanctions according to law.
Article 94 Whoever violates the provisions of this Law, if the act constitutes a crime, shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.
Article 95 Rural residents who work in cities shall participate in social insurance in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 96 Where land owned by rural collectives is expropriated, sufficient social insurance premiums for the peasants whose land is expropriated shall be arranged, and such peasants shall be included in the corresponding social insurance system in accordance with the provisions of the State Council.
Article 97 Foreigners who are employed within the territory of China shall participate in social insurance by reference to the provisions of this Law.
Article 98 This Law shall come into force as of July 1, 2011.
